name: Common Bacterial Blight of Beans
description: A bacterial disease causing leaf spots, blighting, and pod lesions in beans. It is seed-borne and favored by warm, wet conditions, causing significant yield losses in susceptible bean varieties.
symptoms: Large irregular water-soaked lesions on leaves
Lesions turning brown with narrow yellow halos
Water-soaked spots on pods turning reddish-brown
Bacterial ooze from lesions in wet weather
causes: Seed-borne bacteria serving as primary inoculum
Rain splash and wind dispersing bacteria
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides at first symptoms
Remove and destroy infected plant parts
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-legume crops (2+ years)
Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet
Plant resistant bean varieties where available
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
